p01.why: The explicit specialization is in namespace other, which does not enclose lib.

p02.why: A member template's partial specialization can be declared in the class or outside after the enclosing heads, and each use selects as asserted.

p03.why: The declaration fixes two class templates, Outer and Inner, but has only one template <>.

p04.why: A member of an explicitly specialized class is defined with template <>.

p05.why: The explicit specialization of code<int> comes after the call that needs it.

p06.why: Box<bool> has only its own members, so it has no value and has flip.

p07.why: The partial specialization comes after a use that would select it, an error with no diagnostic required; Clang accepts, GCC and EDG reject (Q-0173).

p08.why: Access to the private Owner::Hidden is not checked in the partial specialization's argument list.

p09.why: N + 1 gives no value for N, so N cannot be deduced.

p10.why: Box<int> is declared and not defined, so it is incomplete and its member cannot be accessed.

p11.why: The primary member template is given explicitly for Outer<short>, so the member's partial specialization plays no role there. Clang 18 uses the partial specialization (Q-0206).

p12.why: The global namespace encloses lib, so the qualified explicit specialization is valid.

p13.why: const T* is more specialized than T*, so the values are 1 and 2.

p14.why: Declarations with equivalent heads and argument lists declare the same partial specialization, which is then defined.

p15.why: The member template is specialized for Box<int> and char with two template <>; other uses take the template.

p16.why: The argument list repeats the primary template's parameter list.

p17.why: The variable template's explicit specializations give 1 and 2, and char takes the primary.

p18.why: The given list includes the default int, so Pair<char> matches Pair<T, int>.

p19.why: An explicitly given class has ordinary members that can have default arguments, so get() returns 1 and main returns 0.

p20.why: An explicit specialization has the storage class static.

p21.why: A partial specialization's head can have a pack before other parameters, and the counts are 3 and 2.

p22.why: thread_local is allowed on an explicit specialization, and counter<char> is 1. EDG rejects the declaration (Q-0203).

p23.why: The implicitly declared destructor is explicitly specialized.

p24.why: A function template cannot have a partial specialization. EDG accepts the declaration until a call (Q-0172).

p25.why: No f has a specialization of type int(char*), because f takes two parameters.

p26.why: T* matches int* and const char** (T = const char*), and not int.

p27.why: Box<int> gets its own kind and start, and the other members and Box<char> come from the template, so main returns 0.

p28.why: Kind<int*> uses the partial specialization, which defines pointee.

p29.why: struct and class agree with each other.

p30.why: The class template declares Kind without enumerators, so the explicit specialization can follow the use. GCC rejects every such specialization under -pedantic-errors (Q-0205).

p31.why: U does not appear in the argument list, so deduction cannot find it.

p32.why: Two template <> fix Outer<char> and Inner<int>; the specialized get returns 1 and the other 0, so main returns 0.

p33.why: A member of a member class template given explicitly must be defined with template <> before the template's head.

p34.why: An explicit specialization of a function template has a default argument.

p35.why: The pack T is used in the argument list without ....

p36.why: R(A) matches char(long) with R = char and A = long, and does not match int.

p37.why: auto* P matches only pointer arguments, so kind<1> is 0 and kind<&n> is 1.

p38.why: A partial specialization comes before any declaration of its primary template.

p39.why: Box<int> is declared and not defined, so no object of it can be created.

p40.why: Both partial specializations match Pair<int, int> and neither is more specialized.

p41.why: A friend declaration declares an explicit specialization.

p42.why: Pointer<T> is T*, so the partial specialization matches int* and not int.

p43.why: A friend declaration declares a partial specialization.

p44.why: Traits<void> has its own members, size 0 and marker.

p45.why: An alias template cannot have a partial specialization.

p46.why: The partial specialization's get is declared and never defined, and main calls it.

p47.why: The grid gives these matches: const T matches const int and int* const, T* matches const int*.

p48.why: A thread_local explicit specialization of a thread_local variable template gives 1, and counter<int> is 0.

p49.why: Each kind is defined for its own class, so the values are 1 and 2 and main returns 0.

p50.why: The explicit specialization wins for int*, the partial one for char*, and the primary for int.

p51.why: Access to Owner::Hidden is not checked in the explicit specialization's name.

p52.why: Only an argument of type int fits int V, so 1 selects the partial specialization and 1L and 'c' take the primary. Clang converts and matches (Q-0295).

p53.why: An explicit specialization of a member function template has a default argument.

p54.why: The scoped enumeration is only declared in the class template, so it can be specialized after the use. GCC rejects (Q-0205).

p55.why: The explicit specialization wins for int*, the partial one for char*, and the primary for int.

p56.why: A use through the using-declaration finds partial specializations declared later.

p57.why: Access to Owner::Hidden is not checked in the explicit specialization's function type. GCC checks it and rejects (Q-0204).

p58.why: The partial specialization has no primary template declared before it.

p59.why: union does not agree with the primary template's struct.

p60.why: Same<T, T> needs the same type twice, and int and const int differ.

p61.why: The explicit specialization without an initializer is only a declaration, so count has no definition.

p62.why: The explicit specialization of the static member variable template without an initializer is only a declaration.

p63.why: The enumeration is scoped and no use needed its definition, so it can be specialized after the use. GCC rejects (Q-0205).

p64.why: Plain is not a template, so Plain<int> is not a template-id.

p65.why: The unscoped enumeration is defined in the class template, and the class specialization was used before.

p66.why: The explicit specialization is not inline, and both translation units define it.

p68.why: The reordered list is no more specialized than the primary template. GCC and EDG accept it (Q-0174).

p70.why: &c has type const int*, which fits const auto*, and &n has type int*, which does not, so the values are 1 and 0. Clang 22 converts and matches (Q-0295).

p71.why: An explicit specialization of a member template can be declared in its class. GCC rejects (Q-0171).

p72.why: The explicit specializations for int and char are used, and double takes the template.

p73.why: The partial specialization of the variable template comes after a use that would select it, with no diagnostic required; GCC rejects, Clang and EDG accept (Q-0173).

p74.why: The implicitly declared copy constructor is explicitly specialized.

p75.why: An explicit specialization is declared at block scope.

p76.why: Each explicit specialization has an initializer and is a definition, so the values are 4, 0, and 1.

p77.why: A template <> declaration of one member of Box<char>, which comes from the primary template, has a default argument.

p78.why: The explicit specialization of Box<int> comes after a variable of that type.

p80.why: Giving one partial specialization for Outer<short> keeps the primary and the other partial specialization, so the values are 2, 3, and 0. GCC ignores the explicit one (Q-0207).
